_readme: The per-app band of the homepage: one controller, a dot on each control
the chosen layout uses, and a legend that prints each binding as the app's
own button chips. Logitech's 'App specific customizations' band, with the
marks drawn over the device from data instead of burned into it.
slot   : the RENDER SLOT per family, a fixed 3:2 box. The pictures inside are
stand-ins (manufacturer photos, cut by scripts/pad-cut.py) until the
Blender renders land; a render dropped in must be framed 3:2 with
the controls where `controls` says, or `controls` regenerated.
controls: per family, the centre of each control's mark, as % of the slot
box, set beside the control it names, never on it (a mark on the
glyph hides the glyph). A stick's move and its click are two marks
on two sides of it. `dpad-up` marks the up/down pair, `dpad-left`
and `dpad-right` the left/right pair. Read off a 5% grid
over each pad contained in the 3:2 box (scripts/pad-grid.py
draws them; redraw and re-read if a picture changes). y below 0 is
above the picture. The triggers are behind the bumpers in a front
view, so L2/R2 take the top outer corners, beside the bumpers.
apps   : `groups` in legend order. `hold` is the button kept down for that
group (a ButtonDefs key), null for a plain press; it heads the
group in the legend and is marked at its own `controls` spot. An
item's `c` is its mark, `b` the buttons its chips print (two are
alternatives: up OR down), `fam` limits it to those families. Chip labels come
from scripts/pad-family.js, never from this file.
EVERY LINE IS A CLAIM. Checked 2026-09-27 against ~/Developer/steer:
Default <- SteerCore/Defaults.swift (solo, l1 layers; StickConfig leftMode
.mouse, rightMode .scroll), then Config/ProfileDefaults.swift makeDefault:
a pad with no gyroscope (Xbox) gets the ring on R3 and Mission Control on
L3. Media, Browser <- SteerCore/BundledPresets.swift (BundledPresets.media
/ .browser). Final Cut Pro, Mail <- the same file, BundledAppPresets
.finalCutPro (editorTransportL1, editorEditR2) and .mail. Re-read those
before changing a line; the app's layouts move.
